task_id.description: The task the verdict is on. For a PR that is not a task's (a reconcile, a SPEC or docs PR) it is exactly `pr-<n>`. The record is verification/<task_id>.json.

schema_version.description: SPEC §15.4: the schema version of the ccp that wrote the record (verify.RECORD_VERSION); ccp verify record stamps its own, whatever the input said. A reader older than the record passes over keys its contract does not know, at any depth, and still checks every key it knows. A record without it, or one no newer than the reader, may carry no key the contract does not name.

head_sha.description: The PR head this verdict applies to. ccp verify record requires it on an approve. ccp verify merge-ok requires it and refuses a PR head that differs.

access_mode.description: How the verifier reached the proof surface; the modes of project.schema.json verifier_access.mode

ran.description: False when the verifier did not run this check itself. Such a check is neither a pass nor a fail: pass is null and rests_on names what it rests on, in one of the three forms its description gives (SPEC §15.4).

pass.description: true pass, false fail, null only when ran is false.

rests_on.description: For a check not run: what it rests on. SPEC §15.4: ccp verify record accepts exactly three forms: a ruling, naming spec question ids (sm-…) or gate ids (<task_id>-<n>) that all exist, every gate closed and approved and every spec question answered with verdict resolved; a carried verdict, `approve at <sha>` (§15.6 rule 3), the sha a commit; or, with produced_by operator, any text.

produced_by.description: SPEC §2.3, §15.4: the seat that produced this check's evidence. ccp verify record requires it on every check it writes, except a check closed by a ruling (ran false, rests_on naming the ruling: a ruling is not evidence), which may omit it and must when no evidence underlies the waiver; it refuses evidence produced by a seat that rules on the task (lead, runner) unless operator_step names an approved operator gate. A record written before the field is still read.

operator_step.description: SPEC §15.4: the operator step this evidence came from, as the gate that approved it (escalation id <task_id>-<n>, class operator, decision approved; a standing approval is such a gate). Only then may a ruling seat have produced the evidence.

gate.description: SPEC §15.1: the formal unit/lint gate, as the verifier ran it on head_sha. ccp verify record requires it, every run at exit 0, on an approve, and ccp verify merge-ok refuses an approve without it.

command.description: As run: the product's unit command, its lint command, ccp tasks check, ccp docs check.

modules_ran.description: Deprecated name of ran (a record written before the gate-result contract); read only.

modules_cached.description: Deprecated name of cached (a record written before the gate-result contract); read only.

cold.description: Under plane.json verify.accept_cache: true when the run ignored the cache (the product's cold option).

suite_id.description: SPEC §14.1: the recorded `ccp suite run` of this command. ccp verify record fills exit_code, tests_run, tests_skipped, seconds, ran and cached from it where the entry leaves them out, and a command naming it.

ran.description: Under plane.json verify.accept_cache: the units (tests, modules, files: the product's unit) this run ran (§14.1).

cached.description: Under plane.json verify.accept_cache: the units the product's content-keyed cache reported as hits on identical inputs, which count as run (§14.1).

ci_run.description: Optional: a CI run at the same head the verifier cites beside its own runs, never in place of them.

merge_requested.description: True when verdict=approve. The runner merges once ccp verify merge-ok exits 0 (SPEC §15.1); the verifier never merges.

checked_at.description: The clock time the verdict was reached, as the clock read it: not rounded, not later than the record. ccp verify record stamps it when it is absent and refuses one later than the write.
